# Fireflies meeting → project tag: does Jev earn a place in meeting-sync?

Item #4 of the 2026-09-21 leverage sweep. Its code baseline was measured first
(`docs/FIREFLIES_ATTENDEE_BASELINE.md`): an attendee lookup settles **6%** of 279
meetings, so the item passed gate 3. Eric picked it to start on 2026-09-22 and cleared
Jev to see meeting text as-is, names included.

## Why it would matter

- `meeting-prep` step 2 finds a project's meetings by searching vault notes for the
  project name. The exact name appears in **0 of 279** meetings.
- `status-report` step 2b pulls every meeting in the period; the drafting pass sorts
  them into projects by hand, every two weeks.
- If this passes, `meeting-sync` writes one `project:` line per note, and both skills
  read it. Unsure or unavailable → `project: unfiled`, which is today's state.

## Data handling

Meeting text, names, the label sheet and Jev's raw answers live only in
`fireflies_probe/private/` (gitignored). Committed: code, this doc, aggregate counts.

## Pre-registration (committed before any API call)

**Set.** The 40 most recent meetings in the local Fireflies cache that have a summary
overview: 2026-07-09 to 2026-09-17. Frozen by id in `private/set.json`.

**Options.** All 29 projects in `project-triage/portfolio.json` (name, purpose, charter
receiver where one exists) plus **none of these**. Not only the five chartered ones:
39 of 84 speaker-named meetings pointed at no chartered project, and `meeting-prep`
runs for any project.

**Truth.** Eric labels all 40 **blind** in `private/label_sheet.md`, seeing the title,
date, speakers and overview, before looking at any Jev answer. One project number, two
if a meeting genuinely splits, or 0 for none. Jev is right if its pick is among
Eric's labels.

**Jev.** One Choice per meeting. State: title, date, speakers, keywords, overview,
shorthand bullets, action items. Nothing else.

**Kill test.** Jev goes into `meeting-sync` only if both hold at top probability
**≥ 0.60** ("confident"):

1. **Right on ≥ 90%** of its confident answers.
2. **Confident on ≥ 60%** of the 40 (at least 24).

Otherwise nothing is built, and meetings stay unfiled as today.

**Also reported, not bars:** top-pick accuracy on all 40; a keyword baseline (the
most distinctive project-name words found in the title, overview, bullets and
keywords; a tie or no hit leaves the meeting unsettled). It settles **12 of 40**
before any label exists, so it is a real comparison, not a straw man. There is also an
information-only threshold sweep. **The bar does not move after scoring.**

## Run

```
cd fireflies_probe
python project_tag.py --sheet     # done 2026-09-22
python project_tag.py --collect   # Jev answers -> private/jev.jsonl (do not open)
# Eric fills in private/label_sheet.md
python project_tag.py --score
```

# Fireflies meeting → project tag: does Jev earn a place in meeting-sync?

Item #4 of the 2026-09-21 leverage sweep. Its code baseline was measured first
(`docs/FIREFLIES_ATTENDEE_BASELINE.md`): an attendee lookup settles **6%** of 279
meetings, so the item passed gate 3. Eric picked it to start on 2026-09-22 and cleared
Jev to see meeting text as-is, names included.

## Why it would matter

- `meeting-prep` step 2 finds a project's meetings by searching vault notes for the
  project name. The exact name appears in **0 of 279** meetings.
- `status-report` step 2b pulls every meeting in the period; the drafting pass sorts
  them into projects by hand, every two weeks.
- If this passes, `meeting-sync` writes one `project:` line per note, and both skills
  read it. Unsure or unavailable → `project: unfiled`, which is today's state.

## Data handling

Meeting text, names, the label sheet and Jev's raw answers live only in
`fireflies_probe/private/` (gitignored). Committed: code, this doc, aggregate counts.

## Pre-registration (committed before any API call)

**Set.** The 40 most recent meetings in the local Fireflies cache that have a summary
overview: 2026-07-09 to 2026-09-17. Frozen by id in `private/set.json`.

**Options.** All 29 projects in `project-triage/portfolio.json` (name, purpose, charter
receiver where one exists) plus **none of these**. Not only the five chartered ones:
39 of 84 speaker-named meetings pointed at no chartered project, and `meeting-prep`
runs for any project.

**Truth.** Eric labels all 40 **blind** in `private/label_sheet.md`, seeing the title,
date, speakers and overview, before looking at any Jev answer. One project number, two
if a meeting genuinely splits, or 0 for none. Jev is right if its pick is among
Eric's labels.

**Jev.** One Choice per meeting. State: title, date, speakers, keywords, overview,
shorthand bullets, action items. Nothing else.

**Kill test.** Jev goes into `meeting-sync` only if both hold at top probability
**≥ 0.60** ("confident"):

1. **Right on ≥ 90%** of its confident answers.
2. **Confident on ≥ 60%** of the 40 (at least 24).

Otherwise nothing is built, and meetings stay unfiled as today.

**Also reported, not bars:** top-pick accuracy on all 40; a keyword baseline (the
most distinctive project-name words found in the title, overview, bullets and
keywords; a tie or no hit leaves the meeting unsettled). It settles **12 of 40**
before any label exists, so it is a real comparison, not a straw man. There is also an
information-only threshold sweep. **The bar does not move after scoring.**

## Run

```
cd fireflies_probe
python project_tag.py --sheet     # done 2026-09-22
python project_tag.py --collect   # Jev answers -> private/jev.jsonl (do not open)
# Eric fills in private/label_sheet.md
python project_tag.py --score
```

- **2026-09-22, collect:** 40 of 40 answered, 0 failures. **37 of 40 at top probability
  ≥ 0.60**, so the coverage bar (≥ 24) holds *if* the answers are right. Correctness is
  unknown until Eric labels, and nobody has read the picks.

The Fireflies meeting → project test passed your pre-registered bar. On 39 labelled meetings, Jev was confident on 36 and right on 33 of those (92% on both counts, against bars of 60% and 90%). The keyword baseline was right on only 1 of the 12 meetings it settled.

Most of that pass comes from meetings that aren't about any project:
- **Non-project meetings (28):** Jev agreed on 27 and never confidently put a project tag on one. Tags won't add noise.
- **Project meetings (11):** Jev got 7 right. The four misses:
  - **OKRs_2026-27 (three misses):** twice Jev said "none," and once it picked Education_Curriculum. That pick is defensible, since that project's description names the same 09-02 meeting.
  - **NCAA_BestPractices_Doc:** Jev's pick was below the 0.60 cut-off, so the meeting would simply have stayed unfiled.
- **In practice:** about 2 in 3 project meetings would get the right tag. A wrong tag costs little, because `meeting-prep`'s name search still runs as a fallback. A wrong "none" just leaves the meeting unfiled, which is how every meeting is today.

I haven't changed the OKRs description, because rewriting it and rescoring the same 40 meetings would be tuning on the test set. If you want to try a fuller description, it has to be judged on meetings after 09-17.

Results are in `docs/FIREFLIES_PROJECT_TAG.md`, committed and pushed to draft PR #23 (https://github.com/erash11/TypeSafe_Sandbox/pull/23). Merge #21 first. Your labels are backed up in `TypeSafe_Sandbox\.claude\fireflies_probe_private_backup\`.

---
name: meeting-sync
description: >-
  Sync new Fireflies transcripts into the SecondBrain vault; audit vault filenames for
  drift against Fireflies titles. Idempotent. Use when the user says "sync meetings",
  "pull latest meetings", "/meeting-sync", "update meeting notes", "any new meetings?",
  or when invoked by weekly-review. Also for filename drift — "are any meeting files
  misnamed?", "did a meeting get renamed after export?", "why is this meeting titled
  differently in Fireflies than in the vault?", "audit the meeting filenames". Do not
  use to rename generic titles inside Fireflies (use name-meetings) or to search what
  was said in transcripts (use pp-fireflies).
argument-hint: "[days-back]"
---

# Meeting Sync

Pull new Fireflies transcripts into the SecondBrain vault. Each meeting becomes one markdown file at `Inbox/meetings/YYYY-MM-DD_<title>.md`.

## Paths — shared config

Vault and state-file paths live in `~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.<platform>.json` (single source of truth):
- `vault_inbox_meetings` — platform-specific export target
- `meeting_sync_state_file` — idempotency ledger (`.sync-state.json` in that folder)
- `meeting_lookback_days` — default window (14)

`scripts/sync.py` reads these itself; don't hardcode paths elsewhere. If the vault ever moves, edit the config only.

sync.py passes `--limit 100000` to `transcripts find` — the CLI's default is 100, which silently truncates large backfills. Don't remove that flag.

## Prerequisite — one-time auth

Auth is the `FIREFLIES_API_KEY` environment variable (see the `pp-fireflies` skill's Auth Setup). Verify with `fireflies-pp-cli doctor --agent` — the JSON must show `"auth": "configured"`. `scripts/sync.py` runs this check itself and exits with code 4 if auth is missing. In that case, stop and tell the user:

> Fireflies isn't authenticated yet. Set `FIREFLIES_API_KEY` in your environment (System Properties → Environment Variables on Windows), then restart your terminal. After that, `/meeting-sync` will work.

Do not try to fix auth yourself (no `auth set-token` — the env var is the canonical mechanism). Then exit.

## Sync flow

### 1. Run the pipeline script

The deterministic pipeline (doctor check → CLI sync → find → state diff → export → state update) is fully implemented in `scripts/sync.py`. Two-phase invocation:

**Phase A — list pending, check titles:**
```bash
python scripts/sync.py --list-only [--days-back N]
```
Prints a JSON array of not-yet-exported transcripts: `[{"id", "title", "date"}]`. Diagnostics go to stderr.

**Phase B — export:**
```bash
python scripts/sync.py --no-sync [--days-back N]
```
Prints a JSON array of newly exported absolute file paths (`--no-sync` skips the redundant DB refresh Phase A just did). Exports are detected by diffing the vault directory listing before/after each export — never "most recent .md" — so a no-op export can't claim an unrelated file.

`[days-back]` argument from the user maps to `--days-back N`; otherwise the config default applies.

### 2. Between phases: generic-title judgment (model's job)

The user does not name their Fireflies meetings consistently. Generic titles produce useless filenames in the vault. Check each pending `title` from Phase A against the generic patterns documented in the `name-meetings` skill (empty, `Zoom Meeting`, `Recording`, `Meeting`, date-only, etc.).

- **0 generics:** run Phase B immediately, silently.
- **1–3 generics:** use `AskUserQuestion` once — question: "N of the new meetings have generic titles. Name them before exporting?" with options **[Propose names first / Export as-is]**. If "Propose names first", invoke the `name-meetings` skill scoped to just these IDs, then re-run Phase A to pick up renamed titles before Phase B.
- **4+ generics:** report the count and suggest: *"Several new meetings have generic titles. Run `/name-meetings` to clean them up — I'll proceed with the export either way."* Then run Phase B without blocking.

This keeps the rename loop tight at sync-time without blocking the pipeline.

### 3. Augment each exported file (model's job)

For each path in Phase B's JSON output, the file is raw Fireflies markdown. Insert the fixed 5-section header from `assets/meeting-header.md` (this skill's folder) at the top — after frontmatter, before any existing content. Read the asset and prepend it verbatim.

Leave the Fireflies-generated transcript and summary below this block intact. This gives the user **5 fixed sections to fill in or curate** during interview-me / weekly-review, on top of the raw Fireflies content.

## Drift audit (periodic, not every sync)

A vault filename is a snapshot of the Fireflies title at export time. Titles get renamed afterwards, so the two drift apart. `scripts/audit_filenames.py` detects this by asking the export CLI to regenerate every filename into a scratch dir and diffing against the ledger — **the slug algorithm is never reimplemented**, the CLI is the authority.

```bash
python scripts/audit_filenames.py [--since YYYY-MM-DD] [--skip-linkcheck] [--report PATH]
```

Run it from `weekly-review`, or on demand — **not** on every sync (it spawns one CLI call per ledger entry, ~2-4 min for a full vault). Same exit codes as sync.py; drift itself is not an error, read the counts in the JSON.

It classifies every mismatch, and the classes need different responses:

- **`regression`** — the vault name is good and Fireflies has reverted to an auto-generated stamp (`Jan_19_0445_PM`, `Untitled`, `Audio_Message`). **Never re-export these — it destroys the good name.** Fix the title upstream in Fireflies instead. Note the API refuses title updates on some older meetings; if so, say so and leave the vault alone (the ledger already protects it).
- **`semantic`** — the title genuinely differs in meaning. Usually two generations of AI naming rather than rot, so it needs a human call, not an automatic rename. Surface it, don't act.
- **`cosmetic`** — same words, different separators (`RTP_UpperExtremity` vs `RTP___Upper_Extremity`). Ignore; re-exporting is pure churn.

Before proposing any rename, check `inbound_links` in the output. Renaming a vault file breaks `[[wikilinks]]` from weekly-review notes and `GRAPH_REPORT.md`. Rewrite those links in the same pass or leave the file alone.

## Output to user

When done, report:
- N transcripts found in the window (stderr line from sync.py)
- M new exports written
- Path: `Inbox/meetings/`
- If 0 new: just say "No new meetings since last sync."

Keep it to 3 lines.

## Error handling

sync.py exit codes: 0 ok, 2 usage/config, 3 sync/find failure, 4 auth not configured.

- **Exit 4 (auth):** deliver the auth message from Prerequisite above, stop.
- **Exit 3 (sync/find):** report the stderr error verbatim, do not try to recover. The user may need to refresh their API key.
- **Export fails for one transcript:** sync.py logs a warning to stderr and continues with the rest; relay which one failed.
- **State file corrupted:** sync.py backs it up to `.sync-state.json.bak` and recreates fresh automatically (re-export is idempotent on the filesystem because filenames are deterministic per CLI); flag this in the report if the warning appears.

## What NOT to do

- **Don't re-implement steps the script owns** — doctor, CLI sync, find, state diff, export, state update all live in `scripts/sync.py`.
- **Don't identify exports by "newest .md file"** — that's the exact bug the directory-diff in sync.py fixes.
- **Don't detect filename drift by pattern-matching for "generic-looking" names** — that both misses real drift and invents fake drift. Use `audit_filenames.py`, which compares against what the export CLI actually produces.
- **Don't bulk re-export to "clean up" filenames.** Most mismatches are cosmetic or a second valid naming generation, and the `regression` class gets actively worse. Re-export only what a human approved.
- **Don't modify the Fireflies-generated content** of the exported file — only PREPEND the header from `assets/meeting-header.md`. The transcript and AI summary stay untouched.
- **Don't sync every interaction.** Run sync only when explicitly invoked OR when called by weekly-review / fireflies-intake.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""meeting-sync deterministic pipeline (steps 1-5 of SKILL.md).

Pipeline: doctor auth check -> fireflies-pp-cli sync -> transcripts find
-> state-file diff -> export loop (directory-diff file detection)
-> state-file update.

stdout: a JSON array. Full run: absolute paths of newly exported .md files.
--list-only: pending (not-yet-exported) transcripts as
{"id", "title", "date"} objects, no export performed.
All diagnostics go to stderr.

Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 unexpected, 2 usage/config, 3 sync/find failure,
4 auth not configured.

Paths come from the platform-specific shared config at ../../_shared/.
(vault_inbox_meetings, meeting_sync_state_file, meeting_lookback_days).
"""

import argparse
import json
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

CONFIG_PATH = (
    Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
    / "_shared"
    / ("config.windows.json" if sys.platform == "win32" else "config.macos.json")
)


def log(msg: str) -> None:
    print(msg, file=sys.stderr, flush=True)


def die(code: int, msg: str) -> "None":
    log(f"ERROR: {msg}")
    sys.exit(code)


def load_config() -> dict:
    try:
        with open(CONFIG_PATH, encoding="utf-8") as f:
            cfg = json.load(f)
    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError) as e:
        die(2, f"cannot read shared config {CONFIG_PATH}: {e}")
    for key in ("vault_root", "vault_inbox_meetings", "meeting_sync_state_file"):
        if key not in cfg:
            die(2, f"shared config missing required key: {key}")
    return cfg


def resolve_cli(cfg: dict) -> str:
    configured = cfg.get("fireflies_cli")
    if configured and Path(configured).is_file():
        return str(configured)
    exe = shutil.which("fireflies-pp-cli")
    if not exe:
        die(2, "fireflies-pp-cli not found on PATH")
    return exe


def run_cli(exe: str, args: list, timeout: int = 300) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
    return subprocess.run(
        [exe] + args, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout
    )


def check_auth(exe: str) -> None:
    """Step 1: doctor. Requires JSON field "auth": "configured"
    (key comes from the FIREFLIES_API_KEY environment variable)."""
    proc = run_cli(exe, ["doctor", "--agent"])
    try:
        doc = json.loads(proc.stdout)
    except json.JSONDecodeError:
        die(4, f"doctor output was not JSON (exit {proc.returncode}): "
               f"{proc.stdout[:200]} {proc.stderr[:200]}")
    if doc.get("auth") != "configured":
        die(4, "Fireflies auth not configured. Set FIREFLIES_API_KEY in the "
               "environment (doctor reported auth="
               f"{doc.get('auth')!r}, source={doc.get('auth_source')!r}).")


def refresh_db(exe: str) -> None:
    """Step 2: pull any newly processed transcripts into the local DB."""
    proc = run_cli(exe, ["sync", "--agent"], timeout=600)
    if proc.returncode != 0:
        die(3, f"fireflies-pp-cli sync failed (exit {proc.returncode}): "
               f"{proc.stderr.strip() or proc.stdout.strip()}")


def find_transcripts(exe: str, days_back: int) -> list:
    """Step 3: list processed transcripts in the lookback window."""
    proc = run_cli(exe, [
        "transcripts", "find", "--from", str(days_back),
        "--processed-only", "--json", "--agent",
        # CLI defaults to --limit 100, which silently truncates large
        # backfills (e.g. the 235-meeting ingest); override it.
        "--limit", "100000",
    ])
    if proc.returncode != 0:
        die(3, f"transcripts find failed (exit {proc.returncode}): "
               f"{proc.stderr.strip() or proc.stdout.strip()}")
    try:
        data = json.loads(proc.stdout)
    except json.JSONDecodeError:
        die(3, f"transcripts find output was not JSON: {proc.stdout[:200]}")
    if isinstance(data, dict):
        for key in ("transcripts", "results", "items", "data"):
            if isinstance(data.get(key), list):
                data = data[key]
                break
        else:
            die(3, f"unrecognized find JSON shape: keys={list(data)[:10]}")
    if not isinstance(data, list):
        die(3, "transcripts find JSON is neither a list nor a known wrapper")
    return [t for t in data if isinstance(t, dict) and t.get("id")]


def load_state(state_path: Path) -> dict:
    """Step 4 support: load {"exports": {...}}; back up and recreate if corrupt."""
    if not state_path.exists():
        return {"exports": {}}
    try:
        with open(state_path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
            state = json.load(f)
        if not isinstance(state, dict) or not isinstance(state.get("exports"), dict):
            raise ValueError("missing exports map")
        return state
    except (OSError, ValueError, json.JSONDecodeError) as e:
        bak = state_path.with_suffix(state_path.suffix + ".bak")
        shutil.copy2(state_path, bak)
        log(f"WARNING: state file corrupted ({e}); backed up to {bak.name}, "
            "starting fresh. This run may re-export (filenames are "
            "deterministic, so the filesystem stays idempotent).")
        return {"exports": {}}


def save_state(state_path: Path, state: dict) -> None:
    tmp = state_path.with_suffix(state_path.suffix + ".tmp")
    with open(tmp, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        json.dump(state, f, indent=2)
    tmp.replace(state_path)


def transcript_date(t: dict) -> str:
    return str(t.get("dateString") or t.get("date") or "")


def export_new(exe: str, pending: list, vault: Path,
               state_path: Path, state: dict) -> list:
    """Step 5: export each pending transcript, detecting the written file by
    diffing the vault directory listing before/after each export (never
    "newest .md" — a no-op export must not claim an unrelated file)."""
    exported_paths = []
    for t in pending:
        tid = t["id"]
        before = {p.name for p in vault.glob("*.md")}
        proc = run_cli(exe, [
            "transcripts", "export", tid,
            "--vault", str(vault), "--agent",
        ], timeout=600)
        if proc.returncode != 0:
            log(f"WARNING: export failed for {tid} "
                f"(exit {proc.returncode}): "
                f"{proc.stderr.strip() or proc.stdout.strip()} — continuing.")
            continue
        new_files = [p for p in vault.glob("*.md") if p.name not in before]
        if not new_files:
            log(f"WARNING: export for {tid} reported success but no new file "
                "appeared in the vault; skipping state update to avoid "
                "tagging the wrong file.")
            continue
        if len(new_files) > 1:
            log(f"NOTE: export for {tid} produced {len(new_files)} new files; "
                "using the most recently written one.")
        exported = max(new_files, key=lambda p: p.stat().st_mtime)
        state["exports"][tid] = {
            "filename": exported.name,
            "exported_at": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
        }
        save_state(state_path, state)  # persist per-export: crash-safe
        exported_paths.append(str(exported))
        log(f"exported {tid} -> {exported.name}")
    return exported_paths


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="meeting-sync pipeline")
    parser.add_argument("--days-back", type=int, default=None,
                        help="lookback window in days (default: "
                             "meeting_lookback_days from shared config)")
    parser.add_argument("--list-only", action="store_true",
                        help="print pending (not-yet-exported) transcripts as "
                             "JSON [{id,title,date}] and exit without exporting")
    parser.add_argument("--no-sync", action="store_true",
                        help="skip the fireflies-pp-cli sync refresh (use when "
                             "a sync already ran moments ago, e.g. after "
                             "--list-only)")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    cfg = load_config()
    days_back = args.days_back or int(cfg.get("meeting_lookback_days", 14))
    vault_root = Path(cfg.get("vault_root", ""))
    if not vault_root.is_dir():
        die(2, f"configured vault_root does not exist: {vault_root}")
    vault = Path(cfg["vault_inbox_meetings"])
    state_path = Path(cfg["meeting_sync_state_file"])
    vault.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    exe = resolve_cli(cfg)
    check_auth(exe)
    if not args.no_sync:
        refresh_db(exe)
    transcripts = find_transcripts(exe, days_back)
    state = load_state(state_path)
    pending = [t for t in transcripts if t["id"] not in state["exports"]]
    log(f"{len(transcripts)} transcripts in last {days_back} days; "
        f"{len(pending)} not yet exported.")

    if args.list_only:
        print(json.dumps(
            [{"id": t["id"], "title": t.get("title", ""),
              "date": transcript_date(t)} for t in pending],
            indent=2))
        return 0

    exported = export_new(exe, pending, vault, state_path, state)
    print(json.dumps(exported, indent=2))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

CONFIG_PATH = (
    Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
    / "_shared"
    / ("config.windows.json" if sys.platform == "win32" else "config.macos.json")
)


def log(msg: str) -> None:
    print(msg, file=sys.stderr, flush=True)


def die(code: int, msg: str) -> "None":
    log(f"ERROR: {msg}")
    sys.exit(code)


def load_config() -> dict:
    try:
        with open(CONFIG_PATH, encoding="utf-8") as f:
            cfg = json.load(f)
    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError) as e:
        die(2, f"cannot read shared config {CONFIG_PATH}: {e}")
    for key in ("vault_root", "vault_inbox_meetings", "meeting_sync_state_file"):
        if key not in cfg:
            die(2, f"shared config missing required key: {key}")
    return cfg


def resolve_cli(cfg: dict) -> str:
    configured = cfg.get("fireflies_cli")
    if configured and Path(configured).is_file():
        return str(configured)
    exe = shutil.which("fireflies-pp-cli")
    if not exe:
        die(2, "fireflies-pp-cli not found on PATH")
    return exe


def run_cli(exe: str, args: list, timeout: int = 300) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
    return subprocess.run(
        [exe] + args, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout
    )


def check_auth(exe: str) -> None:
    """Step 1: doctor. Requires JSON field "auth": "configured"
    (key comes from the FIREFLIES_API_KEY environment variable)."""
    proc = run_cli(exe, ["doctor", "--agent"])
    try:
        doc = json.loads(proc.stdout)
    except json.JSONDecodeError:
        die(4, f"doctor output was not JSON (exit {proc.returncode}): "
               f"{proc.stdout[:200]} {proc.stderr[:200]}")
    if doc.get("auth") != "configured":
        die(4, "Fireflies auth not configured. Set FIREFLIES_API_KEY in the "
               "environment (doctor reported auth="
               f"{doc.get('auth')!r}, source={doc.get('auth_source')!r}).")


def refresh_db(exe: str) -> None:
    """Step 2: pull any newly processed transcripts into the local DB."""
    proc = run_cli(exe, ["sync", "--agent"], timeout=600)
    if proc.returncode != 0:
        die(3, f"fireflies-pp-cli sync failed (exit {proc.returncode}): "
               f"{proc.stderr.strip() or proc.stdout.strip()}")


def find_transcripts(exe: str, days_back: int) -> list:
    """Step 3: list processed transcripts in the lookback window."""
    proc = run_cli(exe, [
        "transcripts", "find", "--from", str(days_back),
        "--processed-only", "--json", "--agent",
        # CLI defaults to --limit 100, which silently truncates large
        # backfills (e.g. the 235-meeting ingest); override it.
        "--limit", "100000",
    ])
    if proc.returncode != 0:
        die(3, f"transcripts find failed (exit {proc.returncode}): "
               f"{proc.stderr.strip() or proc.stdout.strip()}")
    try:
        data = json.loads(proc.stdout)
    except json.JSONDecodeError:
        die(3, f"transcripts find output was not JSON: {proc.stdout[:200]}")
    if isinstance(data, dict):
        for key in ("transcripts", "results", "items", "data"):
            if isinstance(data.get(key), list):
                data = data[key]
                break
        else:
            die(3, f"unrecognized find JSON shape: keys={list(data)[:10]}")
    if not isinstance(data, list):
        die(3, "transcripts find JSON is neither a list nor a known wrapper")
    return [t for t in data if isinstance(t, dict) and t.get("id")]


def load_state(state_path: Path) -> dict:
    """Step 4 support: load {"exports": {...}}; back up and recreate if corrupt."""
    if not state_path.exists():
        return {"exports": {}}
    try:
        with open(state_path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
            state = json.load(f)
        if not isinstance(state, dict) or not isinstance(state.get("exports"), dict):
            raise ValueError("missing exports map")
        return state
    except (OSError, ValueError, json.JSONDecodeError) as e:
        bak = state_path.with_suffix(state_path.suffix + ".bak")
        shutil.copy2(state_path, bak)
        log(f"WARNING: state file corrupted ({e}); backed up to {bak.name}, "
            "starting fresh. This run may re-export (filenames are "
            "deterministic, so the filesystem stays idempotent).")
        return {"exports": {}}


def save_state(state_path: Path, state: dict) -> None:
    tmp = state_path.with_suffix(state_path.suffix + ".tmp")
    with open(tmp, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        json.dump(state, f, indent=2)
    tmp.replace(state_path)


def transcript_date(t: dict) -> str:
    return str(t.get("dateString") or t.get("date") or "")


def export_new(exe: str, pending: list, vault: Path,
               state_path: Path, state: dict) -> list:
    """Step 5: export each pending transcript, detecting the written file by
    diffing the vault directory listing before/after each export (never
    "newest .md" — a no-op export must not claim an unrelated file)."""
    exported_paths = []
    for t in pending:
        tid = t["id"]
        before = {p.name for p in vault.glob("*.md")}
        proc = run_cli(exe, [
            "transcripts", "export", tid,
            "--vault", str(vault), "--agent",
        ], timeout=600)
        if proc.returncode != 0:
            log(f"WARNING: export failed for {tid} "
                f"(exit {proc.returncode}): "
                f"{proc.stderr.strip() or proc.stdout.strip()} — continuing.")
            continue
        new_files = [p for p in vault.glob("*.md") if p.name not in before]
        if not new_files:
            log(f"WARNING: export for {tid} reported success but no new file "
                "appeared in the vault; skipping state update to avoid "
                "tagging the wrong file.")
            continue
        if len(new_files) > 1:
            log(f"NOTE: export for {tid} produced {len(new_files)} new files; "
                "using the most recently written one.")
        exported = max(new_files, key=lambda p: p.stat().st_mtime)
        state["exports"][tid] = {
            "filename": exported.name,
            "exported_at": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
        }
        save_state(state_path, state)  # persist per-export: crash-safe
        exported_paths.append(str(exported))
        log(f"exported {tid} -> {exported.name}")
    return exported_paths


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="meeting-sync pipeline")
    parser.add_argument("--days-back", type=int, default=None,
                        help="lookback window in days (default: "
                             "meeting_lookback_days from shared config)")
    parser.add_argument("--list-only", action="store_true",
                        help="print pending (not-yet-exported) transcripts as "
                             "JSON [{id,title,date}] and exit without exporting")
    parser.add_argument("--no-sync", action="store_true",
                        help="skip the fireflies-pp-cli sync refresh (use when "
                             "a sync already ran moments ago, e.g. after "
                             "--list-only)")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    cfg = load_config()
    days_back = args.days_back or int(cfg.get("meeting_lookback_days", 14))
    vault_root = Path(cfg.get("vault_root", ""))
    if not vault_root.is_dir():
        die(2, f"configured vault_root does not exist: {vault_root}")
    vault = Path(cfg["vault_inbox_meetings"])
    state_path = Path(cfg["meeting_sync_state_file"])
    vault.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    exe = resolve_cli(cfg)
    check_auth(exe)
    if not args.no_sync:
        refresh_db(exe)
    transcripts = find_transcripts(exe, days_back)
    state = load_state(state_path)
    pending = [t for t in transcripts if t["id"] not in state["exports"]]
    log(f"{len(transcripts)} transcripts in last {days_back} days; "
        f"{len(pending)} not yet exported.")

    if args.list_only:
        print(json.dumps(
            [{"id": t["id"], "title": t.get("title", ""),
              "date": transcript_date(t)} for t in pending],
            indent=2))
        return 0

    exported = export_new(exe, pending, vault, state_path, state)
    print(json.dumps(exported, indent=2))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

## Customization

**Before executing, check for user customizations at:**
`~/.claude/LIFEOS/USER/CUSTOMIZATIONS/SKILLS/CreateSkill/`

If this directory exists, load and apply any PREFERENCES.md, configurations, or resources found there. These override default behavior. If the directory does not exist, proceed with skill defaults.


## 🚨 MANDATORY: Voice Notification (REQUIRED BEFORE ANY ACTION)

**You MUST send this notification BEFORE doing anything else when this skill is invoked.**

1. **Send voice notification**:
   ```bash
   curl -s -X POST http://localhost:31337/notify \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{"message": "Running the WORKFLOWNAME workflow in the CreateSkill skill to ACTION"}' \
     > /dev/null 2>&1 &
   ```

2. **Output text notification**:
   ```
   Running the **WorkflowName** workflow in the **CreateSkill** skill to ACTION...
   ```

**This is not optional. Execute this curl command immediately upon skill invocation.**

# CreateSkill

Complete skill development lifecycle: **structure** (create, validate, canonicalize) + **effectiveness** (test, improve, optimize triggers). Structural workflows ensure skills follow LifeOS conventions. Effectiveness workflows — inspired by Anthropic's skill-creator — ensure skills actually work and trigger reliably.

## Enforcement

Handrolling skill files — writing `SKILL.md` or `Workflows/`, `Tools/`, `References/` by hand — is forbidden by `skills/CLAUDE.md`. Spawn this skill first and let it orchestrate. Reading these workflows and performing the steps yourself is the exact anti-pattern the rule exists to prevent.

This skill is the **single home** for skill authoring here. `write-a-skill` is a pointer to it; `superpowers:writing-skills` is a third-party plugin skill and is not the authority in this workspace. (Consolidated 2026-08-15.)

*This text used to live in the frontmatter `description`. Descriptions load into every session's system prompt, so enforcement prose belongs in the body — the description now carries only what is needed to trigger.*

## Authoritative Source

**Before creating ANY skill, READ:** `~/.claude/LIFEOS/DOCUMENTATION/Skills/SkillSystem.md`

**Canonical example to follow:** any well-formed public skill in `~/.claude/skills/` (e.g. `Research/SKILL.md`, `Daemon/SKILL.md`, `CreateSkill/SKILL.md` itself).

## Naming Convention — Public vs Private

**Skill name encodes its public/private status. There are exactly two valid forms.**

| Skill type | Directory format | Example | Allowed content |
|------------|------------------|---------|-----------------|
| **Public** | `TitleCase` | `Blogging`, `Daemon`, `CreateSkill` | Templated, safe, generic, ready for public release |
| **Private** | `_ALLCAPS` (underscore prefix, all uppercase) | `<your-release-skill>`, `_INBOX`, `_BROADCAST`, `_DOTFILES` | Anything personal, sensitive, identity-bound, customer-bound, or environment-specific |

**The leading underscore is the public-release boundary.** Release tooling skips `_*` skills entirely — they never leave `~/.claude`. Public skills (no underscore) are mirrored into the LifeOS public release and MUST contain only generic, templated content.

**Sub-file naming (both public and private skills):**

| Component | Format | Example |
|-----------|--------|---------|
| Workflow files | `TitleCase.md` | `Create.md`, `UpdateDaemonInfo.md` |
| Reference docs | `TitleCase.md` | `ProsodyGuide.md`, `ApiReference.md` |
| Tool files | `TitleCase.ts` | `ManageServer.ts` |
| Help files | `TitleCase.help.md` | `ManageServer.help.md` |

**Wrong (NEVER use):**
- Skill dirs: `createskill`, `create-skill`, `CREATE_SKILL` (no underscore + caps for public; no kebab/snake for private)
- Files: `create.md`, `update-info.md`, `SYNC_REPO.md`

### Choosing public vs private — the decision rule

Ask: **"Could this skill be dropped, as-is, into a stranger's `~/.claude/skills/` and just work?"**

- **Yes** → public skill (`TitleCase`). Body must be generic; user-specific config layers in via `LIFEOS/USER/CUSTOMIZATIONS/SKILLS/<SkillName>/`.
- **No, because it references my identity, my contacts, my business, my customer, my paid API, my private infra, my domain, my private repo, my partner, or my financial/health/security data** → private skill (`_ALLCAPS`).

**When in doubt, build it private first (`_ALLCAPS`). Promoting `_FOO` → `Foo` later is easy. Discovering a public skill leaks your life is permanent.**

---

## Public Release Readiness (MANDATORY)

**Public skills (`TitleCase`) ship to the world. Private skills (`_ALLCAPS`) never leave the local repo.** Sensitivity is decided by skill name, not by per-file scrubbing at share-time.

### The Bright Line

**Public skill (`TitleCase`) — content rule:**

ONLY templated, safe, public, ready content. Period.

- ✅ Generic instructions any LifeOS user could follow
- ✅ Templated patterns with placeholders for user-specific values
- ✅ Public API references and dependencies on public tools
- ❌ Real names (people, products, companies, customers)
- ❌ Real domains, hostnames, IPs, internal URLs
- ❌ API keys, tokens, credentials, session cookies, OAuth secrets — even example-looking ones
- ❌ Private repo paths or references (`github.com/<org>/<private-repo>`)
- ❌ Customer data, customer-specific workflows, customer engagement context
- ❌ First-person war stories tied to a specific incident, project, or person
- ❌ User-specific filesystem paths (`/Users/<name>/...`, `/home/<name>/...`)
- ❌ Identity-bound preferences (DA name, principal name, partner name, pet name, financial figures, health data)

**Private skill (`_ALLCAPS`) — content rule:**

Anything goes. Real names, real domains, real customers, real credentials-by-reference (env var names, never values), real war stories, real internal infra. The underscore IS the safety boundary. These skills are excluded from release tooling.

### The Decision Test

When you find yourself wanting to write any of the following into a skill body, that skill MUST be `_ALLCAPS`:

| If the skill mentions… | Skill must be |
|------------------------|---------------|
| A specific person's name (yours, your partner's, your team's, a customer's) | `_ALLCAPS` |
| A specific product name you own or sell | `_ALLCAPS` |
| A specific customer or client | `_ALLCAPS` |
| A specific paid API account, billing realm, or subscription | `_ALLCAPS` |
| A specific private domain, hostname, internal IP, or VPN | `_ALLCAPS` |
| A specific private repo, dotfile location, or local infra | `_ALLCAPS` |
| A specific business process tied to your company | `_ALLCAPS` |
| A specific financial, health, security, or legal context | `_ALLCAPS` |
| A specific incident or one-off war story | `_ALLCAPS` |
| Anything that would be wrong, embarrassing, or unsafe in someone else's `~/.claude/` | `_ALLCAPS` |

If none of the above apply and the skill is fully generic — it can be `TitleCase` (public).

### Where Personal Layering Goes for Public Skills

A public skill can be made user-specific at runtime via `~/.claude/LIFEOS/USER/CUSTOMIZATIONS/SKILLS/<SkillName>/PREFERENCES.md`. The skill body stays generic; the user's customization file overlays per-instance context. Use this when a skill is fundamentally generic but benefits from per-user tweaks (preferred voice, default formats, personal taste).

**Do not use SKILLCUSTOMIZATIONS to smuggle private content into a public skill.** If the skill *requires* private context to function (real customer name, real API account, real internal infra), it is a private skill — name it `_ALLCAPS` and stop.

### Allowed in Public Skills

- Generic `~/` paths (`~/.claude/skills/`, `~/Projects/<tool>/`) — resolve per-user
- Public repo URLs for tools the skill depends on
- Public API endpoints that are conventions, not secrets (e.g., `localhost:31337/notify`)
- Example values clearly marked as placeholders (`<url>`, `<SESSION_ID>`, `test@example.com`)
- Generic env var *names* (never values): `STRIPE_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`

### Pre-Flight Grep (Public Skills Only)

Before shipping or modifying any `TitleCase` skill, run:
```bash
rg -i "<your-name>|<your-org>|<your-product>|<your-domain>|/Users/[a-z]+/" ~/.claude/skills/<SkillName>/
```

Zero matches = ready for public release. Any match = either scrub it, move it to SKILLCUSTOMIZATIONS, or rename the skill to `_ALLCAPS` and stop pretending it's public. **`_ALLCAPS` skills are exempt from this grep — they are private by design.**

---

## Flat Folder Structure (MANDATORY)

**CRITICAL: Keep folder structure FLAT - maximum 2 levels deep.**

### The Rule

**Maximum depth:** `skills/SkillName/Category/`

### ✅ ALLOWED (2 levels max)

```
skills/SkillName/SKILL.md                    # Skill root
skills/SkillName/Workflows/Create.md         # Workflow - one level deep - GOOD
skills/SkillName/Tools/Manage.ts             # Tool - one level deep - GOOD
skills/SkillName/QuickStartGuide.md          # Context file - in root - GOOD
skills/SkillName/Examples.md                 # Context file - in root - GOOD
```

### ❌ FORBIDDEN (Too deep OR wrong location)

```
skills/SkillName/Resources/Guide.md              # Context files go in root, NOT Resources/
skills/SkillName/Docs/Examples.md                # Context files go in root, NOT Docs/
skills/SkillName/Workflows/Category/File.md      # THREE levels - NO
skills/SkillName/Templates/Primitives/File.md    # THREE levels - NO
skills/SkillName/Tools/Utils/Helper.ts           # THREE levels - NO
```

### Allowed Subdirectories

**These subdirectories are allowed:**
- **Workflows/** - Execution workflows ONLY
- **Tools/** - Executable scripts/tools ONLY
- **References/** - Extended reference material for large skills (API docs, detailed guides)

**Context files (documentation, guides, references) go in the skill ROOT or in References/.**

**When to use References/:** When SKILL.md exceeds ~500 lines and has substantial reference content (API signatures, detailed examples, troubleshooting guides). Keep SKILL.md as a routing guide; move encyclopedic content to References/.

### Why

1. **Discoverability** - Easy to find files
2. **Simplicity** - Less navigation overhead
3. **Speed** - Faster file operations
4. **Consistency** - Every skill follows same pattern

**If you need to organize many workflows, use clear filenames instead of subdirectories:**

**See:** `~/.claude/LIFEOS/DOCUMENTATION/Skills/SkillSystem.md` (Flat Folder Structure section)

---

## Dynamic Loading Pattern (Large Skills)

**For skills with SKILL.md > 100 lines:** Use dynamic loading to reduce context on skill invocation.

### How Loading Works

**Session startup:** Only frontmatter loads for routing
**Skill invocation:** Full SKILL.md loads
**Context files:** Load only when workflows reference them

### The Pattern

**SKILL.md** = Minimal (30-50 lines) - loads on skill invocation
- YAML frontmatter with triggers
- Brief description
- Workflow routing table
- Quick reference
- Pointers to context files

**Additional .md files** = Context files - SOPs for specific aspects (loaded on-demand)
- These are Standard Operating Procedures, not just documentation
- They provide specific handling instructions
- Can reference Workflows/, Tools/, etc.

### 🚨 CRITICAL: NO Context/ Subdirectory 🚨

**NEVER create Context/ or Docs/ subdirectories.**

Additional .md files ARE the context files. They live **directly in skill root**.

**WRONG:**
```
skills/Art/
├── SKILL.md
└── Context/              ❌ NEVER CREATE THIS
    └── Aesthetic.md
```

**CORRECT:**
```
skills/Art/
├── SKILL.md
├── Aesthetic.md          ✅ Context file in skill root
├── Examples.md           ✅ Context file in skill root
└── Tools.md              ✅ Context file in skill root
```

**The skill directory IS the context.**

### Example Structure

```
skills/Art/
├── SKILL.md              # 40 lines - minimal routing
├── Aesthetic.md          # Context file - SOP for aesthetic
├── Examples.md           # Context file - SOP for examples
├── Tools.md              # Context file - SOP for tools
├── Workflows/            # Workflows
│   └── Essay.md
└── Tools/                # CLI tools
    └── Generate.ts
```

### Minimal SKILL.md Template

```markdown
---
name: SkillName
description: Create, test, and optimize LifeOS skills — scaffolding, effectiveness testing, description optimization. USE WHEN create skill, new skill, validate skill, test skill, improve skill, optimize description.
---

# SkillName

Brief description.

## Workflow Routing

| Trigger | Workflow |
|---------|----------|
| "trigger" | `Workflows/WorkflowName.md` |

## Quick Reference

**Key points** (3-5 bullet points)

**Full Documentation:**
- Detail 1: `SkillSearch('skillname detail1')` → loads Detail1.md
- Detail 2: `SkillSearch('skillname detail2')` → loads Detail2.md
```

### When To Use

✅ **Use dynamic loading for:**
- SKILL.md > 100 lines
- Multiple documentation sections
- Extensive API reference
- Detailed examples

❌ **Don't use for:**
- Simple skills (< 50 lines)
- Pure utility wrappers (use LIFEOS/TOOLS.md instead)

### Benefits

- **Token Savings:** 70%+ reduction on skill invocation (when full docs not needed)
- **Organization:** SKILL.md = routing, context files = SOPs for specific aspects
- **Efficiency:** Workflows load only what they actually need
- **Maintainability:** Easier to update individual sections

**See:** `~/.claude/LIFEOS/DOCUMENTATION/Skills/SkillSystem.md` (Dynamic Loading Pattern section)

---


## Workflow Routing

### Structure Workflows (scaffolding and conventions)

| Workflow | Trigger | File |
|----------|---------|------|
| **CreateSkill** | "create a new skill" | `Workflows/CreateSkill.md` |
| **ValidateSkill** | "validate skill", "check skill" | `Workflows/ValidateSkill.md` |
| **UpdateSkill** | "update skill", "add workflow" | `Workflows/UpdateSkill.md` |
| **CanonicalizeSkill** | "canonicalize", "fix skill structure" | `Workflows/CanonicalizeSkill.md` |

### Effectiveness Workflows (testing and optimization)

| Workflow | Trigger | File |
|----------|---------|------|
| **TestSkill** | "test skill", "does this skill work", "skill not working" | `Workflows/TestSkill.md` |
| **ImproveSkill** | "improve skill", "skill quality", "fix skill instructions" | `Workflows/ImproveSkill.md` |
| **OptimizeDescription** | "optimize description", "skill not triggering", "trigger accuracy" | `Workflows/OptimizeDescription.md` |

## Skill Types (Choose Before Building)

Before creating any skill, identify which of the 9 types it is (from Anthropic's internal skill taxonomy, Thariq Shihipar, Mar 2026). The type shapes structure and testing decisions.

| Type | Focus | Key Structure | Example |
|------|-------|---------------|---------|
| 1. Library/API Reference | Gotchas, edge cases Claude gets wrong | Lightweight, gotchas-heavy, reference snippets | HonoReference, D1Reference |
| 2. Product Validation | Test/verify code works | State assertions, browser automation, output recording | Browser |
| 3. Data Fetching | Connect to data systems | Credential refs, query patterns, dashboard pointers | USMetrics, _METRICS |
| 4. Business Process | Automate repetitive workflows | Execution logs, consistency tracking | _CLICKUP, _BROADCAST |
| 5. Code Scaffolding | Generate framework boilerplate | Template files, project-aware scripts | CreateCLI, CreateSkill |
| 6. Code Quality | Enforce standards, review | Deterministic scripts, hook integration | /simplify, /code-review |
| 7. CI/CD & Deployment | Deploy with safety patterns | Pre-deploy checks, smoke tests, rollback | (gap — needs Deploy skill) |
| 8. Operations Runbooks | Map phenomena to diagnostics | Phenomenon → tool → query → report | _HEALTHCHECK |
| 9. Infrastructure Ops | Maintenance with safety guardrails | Safety gates, audit logging, orphan detection | _LIFEOS, _DOTFILES |

## Skill Writing Guidance

When writing or improving skill instructions, follow these principles from Anthropic's skill-creator methodology and Thariq Shihipar's "Lessons from Building Claude Code" (Mar 2026):

### Core Principles

- **Don't state the obvious.** Claude is competent at programming and knows codebases. Focus on information that **breaks Claude's default patterns** — things it gets wrong without guidance. Test: "Would Claude do this wrong without being told?" If not, remove it.
- **Explain the why, not just the what.** Models with good theory of mind + clear reasoning outperform models with rigid constraints. Instead of "ALWAYS use 3 bullets", explain why bullets matter for the audience.
- **Keep it lean.** The context window is a public good. Remove instructions that don't improve output. If test transcripts show the agent wasting time on unproductive steps, cut them. SKILL.md should be under 500 lines.
- **Cut intensifier-only lines.** Stating a rule once is the instruction. `MANDATORY`, `CRITICAL`, "not optional", and a third restatement add volume, not constraint — the model obeys specificity and code, not emphasis. Delete any line whose only content is shouting a rule stated elsewhere. Watch `## Best Practices` / `## Tips` sections: they collect default-restating filler ("be thorough", "keep it simple", "validate carefully"). Run the delete-test in `Prompting/Standards.md` § Signal-to-Noise on every line: cut it, and restore only if you can name the specific non-default behavior it forces.
- **Generalize, don't overfit.** Fix underlying patterns, not specific test failures. The skill will be used on many prompts beyond your test set.
- **Bundle repeated work.** If test agents all independently wrote similar helper scripts, add that script to Tools/ so every future invocation benefits.
- **Set appropriate degrees of freedom.** Match specificity to task fragility. Database migrations need exact commands; code reviews need general direction.
- **Don't over-constrain.** Skills are reused heavily. Avoid overly specific instructions. Provide needed information but leave flexibility for different contexts.

### Description Best Practices

- **Descriptions are for models, not humans.** The description is injected into the system prompt. Claude reads it to decide whether to invoke the skill.
- **Descriptions should be slightly pushy.** Models tend to undertrigger. Name specific scenarios even if the user might not explicitly mention the skill.
- **Include negative triggers for confusable skills.** Add "NOT FOR" clauses when skills share vocabulary: `"NOT FOR web pentesting (use WebAssessment)"`.
- **Undertriggering signals:** Skill doesn't load when it should, users manually invoking it.
- **Overtriggering signals:** Skill loads for irrelevant queries, users disabling it.

### Gotchas Section (MANDATORY)

Every skill MUST have a `## Gotchas` section after the workflow routing table. Thariq: "The highest information density in any Skill comes from gotchas sections."

Populate with:
- API quirks Claude doesn't know about
- Common mistakes observed during usage
- Ordering/sequencing requirements that aren't obvious
- Edge cases that cause silent failures

**Gotchas accumulate over time.** After every skill failure, add the lesson.

### BPE (Bitter-Pilled Engineering) Check

Before finalizing any skill, ask: **"Would a smarter model make this skill unnecessary?"**

- **Anti-fragile (keep):** Verification harnesses, data pipelines, tool wrappers, accumulated gotchas, deterministic scripts
- **Fragile (question):** CoT orchestrators, format parsers, retry cascades, elaborate reasoning scaffolding

Focus skills on knowledge Claude can't derive (failure modes, API quirks), tools Claude can't replicate (API calls, automation), and workflows that benefit from consistency.

### Progressive Disclosure (from Anthropic)

Three levels of information loading — use this to manage large skills:
1. **Level 1 (YAML frontmatter):** Always in system prompt. Triggering info only.
2. **Level 2 (SKILL.md body):** Loaded when skill is invoked. Routing + key guidance.
3. **Level 3 (Reference files):** Root-level `.md` files or `References/` subdirectory loaded on demand.

Tell Claude what files exist; it will read them when appropriate. SKILL.md should be under 500 lines — if over, extract detailed content to reference files.

### Testing Best Practices (from Anthropic)

Three testing levels for skills:
1. **Manual testing** — Run queries and observe behavior
2. **Scripted testing** — Automate test cases (use TestSkill workflow)
3. **Programmatic testing** — Build evaluation suites (use Evals skill)

**Evaluation-driven development:** Define what "this skill working" looks like before building the skill. Iterate on a single challenging task until Claude succeeds, then extract the winning approach.

### On-Demand Hook Pattern (from Anthropic)

Skills can include hooks that activate only when invoked, remaining effective for the session:
- `/careful` — Intercept dangerous commands (rm -rf, DROP TABLE, force-push)
- `/freeze` — Block edits outside specific directories
- `/audit` — Log all tool calls for session review

*All guidance above derived from Thariq Shihipar's "Lessons from Building Claude Code" (Mar 2026), Anthropic's official skill guide, and platform documentation.*

## Examples

**Example 1: Create a new skill from scratch**
```
User: "Create a skill for managing my recipes"
→ Invokes CreateSkill workflow
→ Reads SkillSystem.md for structure requirements
→ Creates skill directory with TitleCase naming
→ Creates SKILL.md, Workflows/, Tools/
→ Suggests running TestSkill to verify effectiveness
```

**Example 2: Fix an existing skill that's not routing properly**
```
User: "The research skill isn't triggering - validate it"
→ Invokes ValidateSkill workflow
→ Checks SKILL.md against canonical format
→ Verifies TitleCase naming and USE WHEN triggers
→ Reports compliance issues with fixes
```

**Example 3: Test if a skill actually helps**
```
User: "Test the Blogging skill to see if it's effective"
→ Invokes TestSkill workflow
→ Generates 3 realistic test prompts
→ Spawns with-skill and baseline agents in parallel
→ Compares outputs, presents results
→ Iterates with ImproveSkill based on feedback
```

**Example 4: Skill isn't triggering on relevant prompts**
```
User: "The Security skill doesn't trigger when I ask about pentesting"
→ Invokes OptimizeDescription workflow
→ Generates 20 should/shouldn't-trigger queries
→ Tests description accuracy via subagents
→ Rewrites description, re-tests, reports improvement
```

**Example 5: Improve a skill that produces weak output**
```
User: "The research skill output is too verbose — improve it"
→ Invokes ImproveSkill workflow
→ Reads skill + user feedback
→ Diagnoses root cause (over-specified instructions)
→ Rewrites with reasoning instead of rigid MUSTs
→ Suggests TestSkill to verify improvement
```

## Gotchas

- **Descriptions cap at 1024 chars, and this file's own description sat at ~1022 — 2 to spare** (2026-06-13 audit). It was cut to ~770 on 2026-08-15 by moving enforcement prose to the `## Enforcement` section; every USE WHEN trigger was kept, because descriptions are what make a skill fire. Re-measure before saving any frontmatter edit, and never buy headroom by deleting triggers.
- **Two `## Workflow Routing` headers exist in this file** — the first (~l.284) is inside the embedded template example, the second (~l.323) is the real one. Header-scanning tools must take the LAST match, not the first. Match on line-anchored `^## Workflow Routing`; a plain substring search also hits an inline mention in the UpdateSkill instructions and returns three.
- **Reading this skill's workflows and executing the steps by hand is the handrolling anti-pattern** — `skills/CLAUDE.md` requires invoking the skill, not imitating it. The skill that mandates Gotchas sections went without one until 2026-06-13; treat checklist items as applying to this skill too.

## Execution Log

After completing any workflow, append a single JSONL entry:

```bash
echo '{"ts":"'$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)'","skill":"CreateSkill","workflow":"WORKFLOW_USED","input":"8_WORD_SUMMARY","status":"ok|error","duration_s":SECONDS}' >> ~/.claude/LIFEOS/MEMORY/SKILLS/execution.jsonl
```

Replace `WORKFLOW_USED` with the workflow executed, `8_WORD_SUMMARY` with a brief input description, and `SECONDS` with approximate wall-clock time. Log `status: "error"` if the workflow failed.

# UpdateSkill Workflow

**Purpose:** Add workflows or modify an existing skill while maintaining canonical structure and TitleCase naming.

## Voice Notification

```bash
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:31337/notify \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"message": "Running the UpdateSkill workflow in the CreateSkill skill to modify existing skill"}' \
  > /dev/null 2>&1 &
```

Running the **UpdateSkill** workflow in the **CreateSkill** skill to modify existing skill...

---

## Step 1: Read the Authoritative Source

**REQUIRED FIRST:** Read the canonical structure:

```
~/.claude/LIFEOS/SkillSystem.md
```

---

## Step 2: Read the Current Skill

```bash
~/.claude/skills/[SkillName]/SKILL.md
```

Understand the current:
- Description (single-line with USE WHEN)
- Workflow routing (in markdown body)
- Existing TitleCase naming

---

## Step 3: Understand the Update

What needs to change?
- Adding a new workflow?
- Modifying the description/triggers?
- Updating documentation?

---

## Step 4: Make Changes

### To Add a New Workflow:

1. **Determine TitleCase name:**
   - ✓ `Create.md`, `UpdateDaemonInfo.md`, `SyncRepo.md`
   - ✗ `create.md`, `update-daemon-info.md`, `SYNC_REPO.md`

2. **Create the workflow file:**
```bash
touch ~/.claude/skills/[SkillName]/Workflows/[WorkflowName].md
```

Example:
```bash
touch ~/.claude/skills/_DAEMON/Workflows/UpdatePublicRepo.md
```

3. **Add entry to `## Workflow Routing` section in SKILL.md:**
```markdown
## Workflow Routing

| Workflow | Trigger | File |
|----------|---------|------|
| **ExistingWorkflow** | "existing trigger" | `Workflows/ExistingWorkflow.md` |
| **NewWorkflow** | "new trigger" | `Workflows/NewWorkflow.md` |
```

4. **Write the workflow content**

### To Update Triggers:

Modify the single-line `description` in YAML frontmatter:
```yaml
description: [What it does]. USE WHEN [updated intent triggers using OR]. [Capabilities].
```

### To Add a Tool:

1. **Create TitleCase tool file:**
```bash
touch ~/.claude/skills/[SkillName]/Tools/ToolName.ts
touch ~/.claude/skills/[SkillName]/Tools/ToolName.help.md
```

2. **Ensure Tools/ directory exists:**
```bash
mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills/[SkillName]/Tools
```

---

## Step 5: Verify TitleCase

After making changes, verify naming:

```bash
ls ~/.claude/skills/[SkillName]/Workflows/
ls ~/.claude/skills/[SkillName]/Tools/
```

All files must use TitleCase:
- ✓ `WorkflowName.md`
- ✓ `ToolName.ts`, `ToolName.help.md`
- ✗ `workflow-name.md`, `tool_name.ts`

---

## Step 6: Final Checklist

### Naming
- [ ] New workflow files use TitleCase
- [ ] New tool files use TitleCase
- [ ] Routing table names match file names exactly

### Structure
- [ ] YAML still has single-line description with USE WHEN
- [ ] No separate `triggers:` or `workflows:` arrays in YAML
- [ ] Markdown body has `## Workflow Routing` section
- [ ] All routes point to existing files
- [ ] New workflow files have routing entries

---

## Done

Skill updated while maintaining canonical structure and TitleCase naming.

input.content:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""meeting-sync step 4: tag each exported meeting note with its portfolio project (Jev).

For every note path given, looks up the Fireflies transcript through the sync ledger,
asks TypeSafe's Jev one Choice ("which portfolio project is this meeting mainly about,
or none of these"), and edits only the note's `## Project tags` section:

- confident (top probability >= 0.60) and a project -> adds `- project/<Name>`
- confident "none", or not confident                 -> adds no tag
- either way, adds one `<!-- jev-project: ... -->` line, so a rerun skips the note

Existing tags are never changed or removed. If Jev or the transcript is unavailable,
the note is left untouched (no marker), so a later run retries it. Always exits 0 on
per-note failures: tagging must never block a sync.

The question wording and the 0.60 threshold are the ones measured blind against Eric's
labels on 40 meetings (TypeSafe_Sandbox docs/FIREFLIES_PROJECT_TAG.md, PR #23):
33 of 36 confident answers right. Change them there first, not here.

Usage:
    python scripts/tag_project.py PATH [PATH ...] [--dry-run]

stdout: JSON array of {"path", "choice", "p", "tag"}; diagnostics to stderr.
Exit codes: 0 ok, 2 usage/config.
"""

import argparse
import json
import os
import re
import sqlite3
import sys
import threading
import urllib.request
from datetime import date
from pathlib import Path

CONFIG_PATH = (
    Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
    / "_shared"
    / ("config.windows.json" if sys.platform == "win32" else "config.macos.json")
)
DB_PATH = Path.home() / ".local" / "share" / "fireflies-pp-cli" / "data.db"
ENDPOINT = os.environ.get("TYPESAFE_ENDPOINT", "https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone")
MODEL = os.environ.get("TYPESAFE_MODEL", "jev-latest")
CONFIDENT = 0.60
NONE = "none of these"
MARKER = "<!-- jev-project:"
SECTION = "## Project tags"


def log(msg: str) -> None:
    print(msg, file=sys.stderr, flush=True)


def die(code: int, msg: str) -> "None":
    log(f"ERROR: {msg}")
    sys.exit(code)


def load_config() -> dict:
    try:
        with open(CONFIG_PATH, encoding="utf-8") as f:
            cfg = json.load(f)
    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError) as e:
        die(2, f"cannot read shared config {CONFIG_PATH}: {e}")
    for key in ("meeting_sync_state_file", "portfolio_json"):
        if key not in cfg:
            die(2, f"shared config missing required key: {key}")
    return cfg


def api_key() -> str:
    key = os.environ.get("TYPESAFE_API_KEY", "").strip()
    if key:
        return key
    env_file = Path.home() / ".claude" / "typesafe.env"
    try:
        for line in env_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
            name, _, value = line.strip().partition("=")
            if name.strip() == "TYPESAFE_API_KEY" and value.strip():
                return value.strip().strip("\"'")
    except OSError:
        pass
    return ""


def ask_jev(state: dict, questions: dict, key: str, timeout: float = 30.0) -> dict:
    """One request, real wall-clock timeout (urlopen's timeout is per socket op)."""
    body = json.dumps({"state": state, "model": MODEL, "questions": questions}).encode("utf-8")
    request = urllib.request.Request(
        ENDPOINT, data=body, method="POST",
        headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {key}", "Content-Type": "application/json"},
    )
    outcome = {}

    def perform() -> None:
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=timeout) as response:
                outcome["data"] = json.loads(response.read(8 * 1024 * 1024).decode("utf-8"))
        except BaseException as error:  # noqa: BLE001 - reported by the caller
            outcome["error"] = error

    worker = threading.Thread(target=perform, daemon=True)
    worker.start()
    worker.join(timeout)
    if worker.is_alive():
        raise RuntimeError(f"wall-clock timeout after {timeout}s")
    if "error" in outcome:
        raise RuntimeError(f"{type(outcome['error']).__name__}: {outcome['error']}")
    answer = ((outcome.get("data") or {}).get("answers") or {}).get("project")
    if not isinstance(answer, dict) or not answer.get("probabilities"):
        raise RuntimeError("response carried no project answer")
    return answer


def projects(portfolio: Path) -> list:

    if worker.is_alive():
        raise RuntimeError(f"wall-clock timeout after {timeout}s")
    if "error" in outcome:
        raise RuntimeError(f"{type(outcome['error']).__name__}: {outcome['error']}")
    answer = ((outcome.get("data") or {}).get("answers") or {}).get("project")
    if not isinstance(answer, dict) or not answer.get("probabilities"):
        raise RuntimeError("response carried no project answer")
    return answer


def projects(portfolio: Path) -> list:
    data = json.loads(portfolio.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    items = data.get("projects", data)
    items = items if isinstance(items, list) else list(items.values())
    out = []
    for p in items:
        if not isinstance(p, dict) or not p.get("name"):
            continue
        receiver = (p.get("charter") or {}).get("receiver")
        text = (p.get("purpose") or "").strip()
        if len(text) > 400:
            text = text[:400].rsplit(" ", 1)[0] + "..."
        if receiver:
            text += f" Delivered to: {receiver}."
        out.append({"name": p["name"], "about": text})
    return out


def questions(projs: list) -> dict:
    criteria = {p["name"]: p["about"] or p["name"] for p in projs}
    criteria[NONE] = ("The meeting is mainly about work that is not one of the listed projects: general staff "
                      "business, day-to-day athlete care, a sport's operations, or a project not on this list.")
    return {
        "project": {
            "type": "choice",
            "instructions": (
                "This is the automatic summary of one work meeting recorded by Eric Rash, Director of Applied "
                "Performance at Baylor Athletics. Which one of Eric's projects is this meeting mainly about? "
                "Pick the project the meeting spent the most time moving forward. Choose 'none of these' if "
                "it is mainly about work that is not one of the listed projects."
            ),
            "criteria": criteria,
        }
    }


def meeting_state(r: dict) -> dict:
    s = r.get("summary") or {}
    speakers = sorted({str((x or {}).get("name") or "") for x in (r.get("speakers") or [])
                       if isinstance(x, dict)} - {""})
    return {
        "title": r.get("title") or "",
        "date": (r.get("dateString") or "")[:10],
        "speakers": speakers,
        "keywords": s.get("keywords") or [],
        "overview": s.get("overview") or "",
        "bullets": s.get("shorthand_bullet") or "",
        "action_items": s.get("action_items") or "",
    }


def insert_tag(text: str, tag, marker: str) -> str:
    """Add the tag and marker at the end of the Project tags list, before the next heading."""
    start = text.index(SECTION)
    nxt = re.search(r"^## ", text[start + len(SECTION):], flags=re.M)
    end = start + len(SECTION) + (nxt.start() if nxt else len(text) - start - len(SECTION))
    section = text[start:end].rstrip("\n")
    lines = section.split("\n")
    add = ([f"- project/{tag}"] if tag and f"- project/{tag}" not in lines else []) + [marker]
    return text[:start] + "\n".join(lines + add) + "\n\n" + text[end:].lstrip("\n")


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="tag meeting notes with their portfolio project")
    parser.add_argument("paths", nargs="+")
    parser.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true", help="ask Jev, print results, write nothing")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    cfg = load_config()
    key = api_key()
    if not key:
        log("WARNING: no TYPESAFE_API_KEY (env or ~/.claude/typesafe.env); notes left untagged.")
        print("[]")
        return 0
    ledger = json.loads(Path(cfg["meeting_sync_state_file"]).read_text(encoding="utf-8")).get("exports", {})
    by_file = {v.get("filename"): tid for tid, v in ledger.items()}
    projs = projects(Path(cfg["portfolio_json"]))
    qs = questions(projs)
    db = sqlite3.connect(DB_PATH)

    results = []
    for raw in args.paths:
        path = Path(raw)
        try:
            with open(path, encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f:
                original = f.read()
        except OSError as e:
            log(f"WARNING: cannot read {path}: {e}")
            continue
        eol = "\r\n" if "\r\n" in original else "\n"  # keep the file's own line endings
        text = original.replace("\r\n", "\n")
        if MARKER in text:
            log(f"skip (already checked): {path.name}")
            continue
        if SECTION not in text:
            log(f"skip (no '{SECTION}' header yet; prepend the header first): {path.name}")
            continue
        tid = by_file.get(path.name)
        row = db.execute("select data from transcripts where id = ?", (tid,)).fetchone() if tid else None
        if not row:
            log(f"skip (no transcript for this file in the ledger/DB): {path.name}")
            continue
        try:
            answer = ask_jev({"meeting": meeting_state(json.loads(row[0]))}, qs, key)
        except RuntimeError as e:
            log(f"WARNING: Jev unavailable for {path.name}: {e}; left untagged, will retry next run.")
            continue
        choice = answer.get("choice")
        p = round(max(answer["probabilities"].values()), 2)
        tag = choice if (p >= CONFIDENT and choice != NONE) else None
        marker = f"{MARKER} {choice} p={p} {date.today().isoformat()}{'' if p >= CONFIDENT else ' (unsure)'} -->"
        if not args.dry_run:
            path.write_text(insert_tag(text, tag, marker), encoding="utf-8")
        results.append({"path": str(path), "choice": choice, "p": p, "tag": tag})
        log(f"{'would tag' if args.dry_run else 'tagged'} {path.name}: {tag or '-'} ({choice}, p={p})")
    print(json.dumps(results, indent=2))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
