Base directory for this skill: C:\Users\eric_rash\.claude\skills\closeout

# Closeout

One command that replaces the manual end-of-day sequence: "any loose ends?" → "commit and push what needs to be" → "is this in memory?" → "write a handoff so Codex can pick this up."

Run all five checks, then give ONE verdict. Do not ask permission between steps — the invocation of this skill IS the authorization for the full sequence. Commit and push is standing-authorized for every DEV repo: each repo's `AGENTS.md` Session routine says "update STATUS, commit, push at end", and unpushed work on one machine is the top cause of conflicts on the other. The only exceptions are repos whose `CLAUDE.md` says their data must stay local (DexaProject is the precedent); commit those locally and list them as open.

This one file serves Claude Code, Codex and Cowork (uploaded to claude.ai). Cowork has no TaskList and no Claude Code memory hooks: do what applies there and say what was skipped.

## Step 1 — Loose-ends sweep

- `git status` across **every** repo in DEV, not only the ones named in this conversation. Another session, another harness, or the other machine may have left work dirty, and a closeout that only checks what it remembers touching will say "clear to sign off" over someone else's uncommitted work. Walk `DEV/`, `DEV/Football/` and `DEV/SpecialRequests/`, and report any repo with uncommitted or unpushed commits. The full walk takes about 90 seconds.
  - Windows: `git -C <repo> status --porcelain` per repo. Do NOT use `Get-ChildItem -Recurse` to look for files; it silently skips paths past the 260-character limit. Inside a repo, `git ls-files` is the reliable way to ask whether a file exists.
  - Repos with dirty state you did not touch: commit and push them like any other, and name them in the report so the user knows another session left them.
- Unfinished todos/tasks from this session (TaskList if available).
- Background jobs or workflows still running.
- Anything the user was promised earlier in the session that wasn't delivered.

## Step 2 — Commit & push

- Every repo touched this session: stage, commit with a descriptive message, `git pull --no-rebase` (the other machine may have pushed), push. If the merge conflicts, follow the conflict steps in `dev-sync/SKILL.md` (they are the one home for them), then push and list the file under "Still open".
- Before staging, make sure any new file over 95 MB and any `.env` is in `.gitignore`.
- Local-only repos (CLAUDE.md says so): commit, do not push, list it.
- Also check the three config repos, `~/.claude` (dotclaude), `~/.claude/skills` (claude-skills) and `~/.claude/global-memory` (claude-global-memory). If any has changes, commit and push it the same way, so the other machine's `/dev-sync` picks it up.
- **Push `global-memory` even on a light session.** `daily-backup` pushes it nightly, which is too late for a same-day handoff: work the Mac in the afternoon, sit down at Windows that evening, and anything written to MEMORY.md or handoffs is still only on the Mac. Pushing it here is what makes memory available to the other machine tonight rather than tomorrow. It is the only repo that carries memory across, so treat an unpushed `global-memory` the same as an unpushed project repo: it blocks "clear to sign off".
- Nothing to commit → say so in one line, move on.

## Step 3 — Memory verification

- Check `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log` — must be empty. If not, surface contents and fix the hook issue if obvious.
- Confirm today's transcript file exists at `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/<today>.md` and was modified within the last few hours. On a Cowork-only day it may be absent; say so, it is not an error.
- Run the dev-docs harvest so repo docs reach memsearch: `bash ~/.claude/scripts/harvest-dev-docs.sh` (Mac) or `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $HOME\.claude\scripts\harvest-dev-docs.ps1` (Windows). It copies every repo's `docs/*.md` into `~/.claude/global-memory/dev-docs/`, which is on the index list. One line of output; do this after Step 4 so today's STATUS is included.
- If this session produced a durable decision or new active thread, update `~/.claude/global-memory/MEMORY.md` (respect the 2,500-char cap; consolidate before adding) or write a Tier A memory file per the memory-system rules in CLAUDE.md.
- **Tier A does not cross machines — mirror it or lose it.** Project memory lives under a slug built from the project's absolute path, and that path differs on the Mac and the Windows laptop, so a Tier A file written today is not auto-injected tomorrow on the other machine. Global memory and the repo both cross; Tier A does not. So for every Tier A fact written this session, ask: is this durable and project-scoped? If yes, it must also land in the repo — `docs/STATUS.md` for current state, `docs/DECISIONS.md` for a decision and its reasoning, the dated handoff for the detail. Treat Tier A as a fast local cache and the repo as the record. If a fact only ever exists in Tier A, assume the other machine will never see it.

## Step 4 — Cross-harness handoff

This is the **canonical durable handoff** — the one future sessions and other harnesses read. (For a mid-session, chat-only summary before `/clear`, that's the `session-handoff` skill; the mattpocock `handoff` skill writes to the OS temp dir and is not durable — don't rely on it for cross-session state.)

If real work happened this session (not just Q&A), write a handoff to
`<repo>/docs/handoffs/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.md` (or `~/.claude/global-memory/handoffs/` if no repo fits):

- What was being worked on and why
- Decisions made (with the reasoning that would be lost)
- Exact file paths of everything created or modified this session
- Next actions, most important first
- Anything mid-flight (open questions, awaited inputs)

Plain markdown, no harness-specific syntax — Codex, Antigravity, or a fresh Claude session must be able to resume from it. Commit it with the Step 2 commit when in a repo.

**Always, in every repo touched (even for light sessions): update `docs/STATUS.md`.** It is the file the next session reads first, on either machine, in any harness. Rewrite the sections in place, keep it short:

- `## Current state` — two to five lines on where things stand today
- `## Next` — most important first
- `## Open questions` — decisions waiting on Eric
- `## Gotchas` — anything that will bite the next session

The dated handoff file is the detailed record; STATUS.md is the summary. Do Step 4 before the Step 2 commit so both land in the same push.

## Step 5 — Verdict

End with a single short report:

```
## Closeout — <date>

**Committed & pushed:** <repos + one-line summary, or "nothing to commit">
**STATUS.md:** updated in <repos>
**Memory:** captured ✓ / issue found: <what> / skipped (Cowork, no hooks)
**Handoff:** <path, or "not needed — no substantive work">
**Still open:** <numbered list, or "none">

Clear to sign off. / Not clear: <the one thing blocking>.
```

"Clear to sign off" means: every touched repo is pushed (or is a declared local-only repo). If anything is unpushed, the verdict is "Not clear" and the unpushed repo is the one thing blocking.

Every file created or modified during the session must appear somewhere in the report with its full path — "where did this save?" should never need to be asked.

## Rules

- Push every touched DEV repo. Do not leave the laptop with unpushed work; the other machine pulls from GitHub, not from this disk.
- Never skip Step 3 — memory capture failing silently is the user's top recurring worry.
- If a check fails and the fix is quick and safe (restage a file, clear a stale lock), fix it and note it. If the fix is risky, list it under "Still open" instead.
- Total output should fit on one screen. The user is leaving; brevity is the deliverable.

# 2026-09-22 — the DB left the repo, and the machines now trade Parquet

## What happened and why

A `--season 2026` pull was killed when the machine ran out of memory. Investigating it
turned up the real problem: **Google Drive had `pff.db` open.** `~/Desktop/DEV` is a
two-way Drive mirror, so every write to the 542 MB database made Drive re-read,
re-upload and lock the whole file. The error was plain in the logs:

    File is already open in GoogleDriveFS.exe (PID 16812)

The same investigation explained a separate complaint (about 2,900 Drive sync errors):
`DEV\.tmp.driveupload` held **10,704 files, 3.2 GB, every one read-only** — Drive's own
staging copies of the renv R library, which renv marks read-only. Windows will not let
`DeleteFileW` remove a read-only file, so Drive retried ~10,700 times an hour. Clearing
the read-only attribute let Drive clean up; a Drive restart then showed **0 errors** and
reclaimed 3.2 GB.

## Decisions, with the reasoning that would otherwise be lost

1. **The DB stays local, on purpose.** Every consumer is a single-analyst, read-only,
   scan-heavy query; 6 M rows is small for DuckDB; the API is the system of record so
   the file is a cache, not data at risk; and it is licensed PFF data, so keeping it off
   third-party cloud avoids a contract and IT question entirely.
2. **But it must not live in a synced folder.** `$PFF_DB` gives it one home per machine
   (Windows `%LOCALAPPDATA%\pff-data\pff.db`). The old path stays as the fallback so an
   unconfigured machine, including the Mac, behaves exactly as before. This mirrors the
   renv fix Eric made the same day (`RENV_PATHS_LIBRARY_ROOT`).
3. **Machines exchange immutable Parquet, never a database.** Written once and never
   mutated, so a half-synced file cannot corrupt anything — which a live `.db` on Drive
   demonstrably can. One file per table per season keeps a single season cheap to move.
4. **`ingest_log` is never exported.** It records what *this* machine fetched; copying it
   would make the other machine's history a lie.

## Files created or modified

- `src/db.py` — `DEFAULT_DB_PATH` now reads `$PFF_DB` (PR #1)
- `src/snapshot.py` — new: snapshot layout, manifest merge, default Drive root (PR #2)
- `scripts/export_snapshot.py`, `scripts/load_snapshot.py` — new (PR #2)
- `tests/test_snapshot.py` — new, 8 tests (PR #2)
- `AGENTS.md` + `CLAUDE.md` — DB location gotcha and a "Moving data between machines"
  section (the repo's pre-commit hook requires the two files to stay byte-identical)
- `docs/STATUS.md` — this state
- Moved on disk, not in git: `pff.db` and its backup to
  `C:\Users\eric_rash\AppData\Local\pff-data\`
- Written to Drive: `G:\My Drive\00_Primary_Storage_Drive\pff-snapshots\` — 22 files,
  6,680,487 rows, 40 MB

Companion changes in the consumer repos: `SpringPlayerEvals_SymAnalysis` PR #1 and
`PlayCalls_SuccessRate_EPA` PR #1, both resolving `$PFF_DB` the same way. PlayCalls had
the **Mac** path hardcoded in two places, so it could never have run on Windows.

## Verification actually performed

- The path resolves with and without `$PFF_DB`; the DB opens from its new home.
- After the move, the file's lock holder is the pipeline's own python process rather
  than `GoogleDriveFS.exe`.
- Exported 2026, loaded it into an empty DB: counts match the manifest exactly. Reran
  the load: no duplication. Dry-run against the live DB: "same" for all 22 files.
- A test found a real bug: with a plain `INSERT`, one primary key that already existed
  locally under a different season aborted the whole file. Now `INSERT OR REPLACE`.
- 8 new tests pass; 43 of the suite passes. `tests/test_season_plays.py` cannot be
  collected on this machine because `ijson` is not installed — pre-existing, unrelated.

## Next actions

1. **Mac:** `git pull`, then `python scripts/load_snapshot.py`. That takes 2026 from
   Drive with no API calls.
2. **Mac, afterwards:** export the video-play data (the 09-13 ingests) so Windows can
   load it. Windows has never had it.
3. Weekly during the season: `python run_pipeline.py --season 2026`, then
   `export_snapshot.py --season 2026` so the other machine can follow.

## Mid-flight

- Nothing is running. The 2026 pull finished cleanly (exit 0).
- `$PFF_DB` is deliberately **not** set on the Mac. Set it only if the Mac's `~/DEV` is
  also inside a synced folder; nobody has checked that yet.

cd ~/DEV/Football/PFF_Data_Project

git log --oneline -1
ls scripts/
```

What I expect: the branch line says something other than `main`, and `ls scripts/` shows only `phase0_probe.py`, `pull_season_video_plays.py` and `pull_video_plays.py`.

If the branch isn't `main`, this fixes it:

```
git checkout main && git pull
ls scripts/
```

You should then see `export_snapshot.py` and `load_snapshot.py`, and `git log --oneline -1` should show commit `e494290` or newer. After that:

```
python3 scripts/load_snapshot.py --dry-run
```

I used `python` earlier; on your Mac it's probably `python3`. The dry run just reports what would change, so it's safe either way.

One other possibility worth ruling out while you're there: if `git pull` printed an error about local changes rather than updating, `git status --short` will show it, and nothing would have arrived.

# 2026-09-22 — the first Jev item to ship, and the ninth to be measured off the map

Two items from the 2026-09-21 leverage sweep were run end to end. One passed and is in
production; one failed by 0.002 and was not built. Eric cleared Jev to read meeting and
note text as-is, names included, which removed the stripping step both items carried.

## 1. Fireflies meeting → project tag — PASSED and SHIPPED

**Why it qualified.** The sweep's gate needs a fuzzy answer, an existing consumer, and a
code baseline measured first. The baseline was measured and failed: an attendee lookup
settles **6%** of 279 meetings (`docs/FIREFLIES_ATTENDEE_BASELINE.md`), and the exact
project name appears in **0 of 279** meetings, which is what `meeting-prep` step 2
searches for.

**Test, pre-registered in `e753cc6` before any call.** 40 most recent meetings with a
summary; one Choice over all 29 `portfolio.json` projects plus "none of these"; bar =
right on ≥ 90% of confident answers (top probability ≥ 0.60) and confident on ≥ 60%.

**Result: PASS.** Eric labelled 39 of 40 blind. Jev was confident on 36/39 (92%) and
right on 33/36 (92%). The keyword baseline settled 12 and was right on **1**.

**Read it honestly.** 28 of 39 meetings were "none of these", and Jev got 27 of those,
never confidently tagging a non-project meeting. On the 11 real project meetings it was
right on **7**. OKRs_2026-27 is 3 of the 4 misses, because its portfolio purpose is one
line and an umbrella planning meeting has nothing to match against. Rewriting that
purpose must be judged on meetings after 2026-09-17, not on these 40.

**Shipped** as `meeting-sync` step 4 (`scripts/tag_project.py`, claude-skills PR #1,
merged `2da77af`), with `meeting-prep` reading the tag and keeping its text-search
fallback. Live on Windows; the Mac pulled `~/.claude/skills` the same day.

**Backfill over the vault:** 246 notes marked, **14 tagged**, 206 confident "none", 26
unsure, 260 lines added and **0 removed** (SecondBrain `43ef103`). A 14-tag yield is low
and is not a failure of the tagger: most of the meeting history is recruiting calls,
vendor demos and staff business belonging to no portfolio project, which matches Eric's
own labels. The payoff is on new meetings.

**Design decisions worth keeping.** Append-only, never editing the 88 notes that carry
hand tags in a different vocabulary (`project/rtp`). One `<!-- jev-project: -->` marker
per note, so a rerun skips it and the answer is auditable. Fails open: no key, no
network or no transcript leaves the note untouched for a later run. A bug found in
testing: an early draft normalised line endings and rewrote ~50 lines of a note that
mixes CRLF and LF; the shipped version splices in only its own lines.

## 2. Spring exit notes → trajectory — FAILED by 0.002, not built

**Pre-registered in `93c4120`**: four department Scores (position coach, strength,
nutrition, academics) weighted PC .50 / STR .20 / N .15 / AC .15 into a continuous
composite. Bars: rho ≥ 0.30 against blended snaps on the same 34 athletes the Claude
pass was scored on, and rho ≥ 0.95 between two independent runs.

**Result: rho 0.298** (n 34, p 0.087) against a 0.30 bar. Claude pass 0.352, keyword
rubric 0.218. **Stability rho 0.998** over two runs of all 99, 96/99 in the same bin.

At n=34 the CI is roughly ±0.33, so 0.298 and 0.352 cannot be separated — but a
near-miss is still a miss, and rerunning with new weights until it clears is the tuning
this project refuses. The bar was not moved. The Claude pass stays; `coach_pdf.py` is
untouched.

**The finding worth keeping is role, not trajectory.** The role Score was held out of
the composite on purpose and reaches **rho 0.643** (n 34). The assumption that role is
mere extraction was checked and is **wrong**: only **5 of 99** notes carry a literal
"Role =", and role words anywhere in the coach note settle 16/34 at rho 0.405 (n.s.)
where Jev reaches 0.664 on those same 16 (p 0.005) and covers all 34. That was measured
after the fact on the same athletes, so it does **not** convert the failure into a pass.
It earns its own pre-registered test.

## Files created or modified

- `fireflies_probe/project_tag.py`, `docs/FIREFLIES_PROJECT_TAG.md` (PR #23)
- `spring_notes/trajectory.py`, `spring_notes/role_baseline.py`,
  `docs/SPRING_NOTES_TRAJECTORY.md` (PR #25)
- `docs/STATUS.md` — both results
- `.gitignore` — `fireflies_probe/private/`, `spring_notes/private/`
- Outside this repo: `claude-skills` `meeting-sync/scripts/tag_project.py` and
  `meeting-sync/SKILL.md` step 4 + Gotchas, `meeting-prep/SKILL.md` step 2
- Private, gitignored, never committed: `fireflies_probe/private/` (label sheet, Jev
  answers, frozen set), `spring_notes/private/` (two runs over 99 athletes). A copy of
  the labelled Fireflies sheet is in `TypeSafe_Sandbox/.claude/fireflies_probe_private_backup/`.

## Next actions

1. **The role test against 2026 snaps.** Pre-register before looking: the target is
   2026 playing time, which is genuinely forward-looking, unlike the 2023-2025 blend
   this test used. PFF 2026 data is now on this machine (weeks 0-3) and on Drive as a
   Parquet snapshot. **Sharper around week 8** than on 3 games.
2. Watch the first real `/meeting-prep` run that uses a `project:` tag, and check it
   finds meetings the old name search missed.
3. Leave the OKRs_2026-27 purpose alone until there are post-09-17 meetings to judge a
   rewrite on.

## Mid-flight

- Nothing running. All three PRs (#21, #23, #25) merged.
- Ten items have now been through the gate: one shipped (this meeting tag), nine
  measured off the map. The gate is doing its job, and the one that passed is the one
  whose code baseline had already been measured and failed.

# 2026-09-22 — the first Jev item to ship, and another measured off the map

Two items from the 2026-09-21 leverage sweep were run end to end. One passed and is in
production; one failed by 0.002 and was not built. Eric cleared Jev to read meeting and
note text as-is, names included, which removed the name-stripping step both items
carried in the sweep.

## 1. Fireflies meeting → project tag — PASSED and SHIPPED

**Why it qualified.** The gate needs a fuzzy answer, an existing consumer, and a code
baseline measured first. That baseline was measured and failed: an attendee lookup
settles **6%** of 279 meetings (`docs/FIREFLIES_ATTENDEE_BASELINE.md`), and the exact
project name appears in **0 of 279** meetings, which is what `meeting-prep` step 2
searches for.

**Test, pre-registered in `e753cc6` before any call.** The 40 most recent meetings with a
summary; one Choice over all 29 `portfolio.json` projects plus "none of these"; bar =
right on ≥ 90% of confident answers (top probability ≥ 0.60) and confident on ≥ 60%.

**Result: PASS.** Eric labelled 39 of 40 blind. Jev was confident on 36/39 (92%) and
right on 33/36 (92%). The keyword baseline settled 12 and was right on **1**.

**Read it honestly.** 28 of 39 meetings were "none of these", and Jev got 27 of those,
never confidently tagging a non-project meeting. On the 11 real project meetings it was
right on **7**. OKRs_2026-27 accounts for 3 of the 4 misses, because its portfolio
purpose is one line and an umbrella planning meeting has nothing to match against.
Rewriting that purpose has to be judged on meetings after 2026-09-17, not on these 40.

**Shipped** as `meeting-sync` step 4 (`scripts/tag_project.py`, claude-skills PR #1,
merged `2da77af`), with `meeting-prep` reading the tag and keeping its text search as a
fallback. Live on Windows; the Mac pulled `~/.claude/skills` the same day.

**Backfill over the vault:** 246 notes marked, **14 tagged**, 206 confident "none", 26
unsure, 260 lines added and **0 removed** (SecondBrain `43ef103`). A 14-tag yield is low
and is not a failure of the tagger: most of the meeting history is recruiting calls,
vendor demos and staff business that belongs to no portfolio project, which matches
Eric's own labels. The payoff is on new meetings.

**Design decisions worth keeping.** Append-only, never touching the 88 notes that carry
hand tags in a different vocabulary (`project/rtp`). One `<!-- jev-project: -->` marker
per note, so a rerun skips it and every answer is auditable. Fails open: no key, no
network or no transcript leaves the note untouched for a later run. A bug found in
testing: an early draft normalised line endings and rewrote about 50 lines of a note
that mixes CRLF and LF. The shipped version splices in only its own lines.

## 2. Spring exit notes → trajectory — FAILED by 0.002, not built

**Pre-registered in `93c4120`**: four department Scores (position coach, strength,
nutrition, academics) weighted PC .50 / STR .20 / N .15 / AC .15 into a continuous
composite. Bars: rho ≥ 0.30 against blended snaps on the same 34 athletes the Claude
pass was scored on, and rho ≥ 0.95 between two independent runs.

**Result: rho 0.298** (n 34, p 0.087) against the 0.30 bar. Claude pass 0.352, keyword
rubric 0.218. **Stability rho 0.998** across two runs of all 99, 96/99 in the same bin.

At n=34 the confidence interval is roughly ±0.33, so 0.298 and 0.352 cannot be
separated — but a near-miss is still a miss, and rerunning with new weights until it
clears is the tuning this project refuses. The bar was not moved. The Claude pass stays
and `coach_pdf.py` is untouched.

**The finding worth keeping is role, not trajectory.** The role Score was held out of
the composite on purpose and reaches **rho 0.643** (n 34). The assumption that role is
mere extraction was checked and is **wrong**: only **5 of 99** notes carry a literal
"Role =", and role words anywhere in the coach note settle 16/34 at rho 0.405 (not
significant) where Jev reaches 0.664 on those same 16 (p 0.005) and covers all 34. That
was measured after the fact on the same athletes, so it does **not** convert the failure
into a pass. It earns its own pre-registered test.

## Files created or modified

- `fireflies_probe/project_tag.py`, `docs/FIREFLIES_PROJECT_TAG.md` (PR #23)
- `spring_notes/trajectory.py`, `spring_notes/role_baseline.py`,
  `docs/SPRING_NOTES_TRAJECTORY.md` (PR #25)
- `docs/STATUS.md` — both results
- `.gitignore` — added `fireflies_probe/private/` and `spring_notes/private/`
- Outside this repo: claude-skills `meeting-sync/scripts/tag_project.py`,
  `meeting-sync/SKILL.md` (step 4 + Gotchas), `meeting-prep/SKILL.md` (step 2)
- Private, gitignored, never committed: `fireflies_probe/private/` (label sheet, Jev
  answers, frozen set) and `spring_notes/private/` (two runs over 99 athletes). A copy
  of the labelled Fireflies sheet is in
  `TypeSafe_Sandbox/.claude/fireflies_probe_private_backup/`.

## Next actions

1. **The role test against 2026 snaps.** Pre-register before looking. The target is 2026
   playing time, which is genuinely forward-looking, unlike the 2023-2025 blend this
   test used. PFF 2026 data is on this machine (weeks 0-3) and on Drive as a Parquet
   snapshot. It will be **sharper around week 8** than on 3 games.
2. Watch the first real `/meeting-prep` run that uses a `project:` tag and check it finds
   meetings the old name search missed.
3. Leave the OKRs_2026-27 purpose alone until there are post-09-17 meetings to judge a
   rewrite against.

## Mid-flight

- Nothing running. PRs #21, #23 and #25 are merged.
- The gate has now taken ten items: one shipped (this tag), nine measured off the map.
  The one that passed is the one whose code baseline had already been measured and
  failed, which is the pattern to keep selecting on.

# STATUS

## Current state (2026-09-22)
- **The Claude pass stays.** A Jev alternative to `semantic_scores.json` was measured
  and **failed**: four department Scores combined in code reach **rho 0.298** against
  blended snaps on the same 34 athletes, versus a pre-registered 0.30 bar. The Claude
  pass is 0.352, the Excel keyword rubric 0.218. At n=34 the CI is about ±0.33, so 0.298
  and 0.352 cannot really be separated, but the bar was not moved. `coach_pdf.py` and
  the locked schema are untouched. Full write-up:
  `TypeSafe_Sandbox/docs/SPRING_NOTES_TRAJECTORY.md`.
- **Worth knowing for next spring:** the Jev scorer reruns and gives the same answer
  (stability rho 0.998 over two runs of all 99), which the one-off Claude pass cannot.
- **Depth-chart role is the live thread, not trajectory.** A held-out role Score hits
  **rho 0.643** against snaps. Only 5 of 99 notes state a role literally, and keyword
  matching settles 16/34 at rho 0.405, so this is not extraction a regex can do.
- `src/config.py` now reads the PFF DuckDB path from **`$PFF_DB`**, falling back to the
  old literal path. The DB moved out of the Drive-mirrored DEV tree the same day.

## Next
1. Pre-register a role-vs-**2026**-snaps test before looking at any result. 2026 PFF data
   is pulled through week 3; it will be sharper around week 8 than on 3 games.
2. Nothing else is in flight here.

## Open questions
- None waiting on Eric.

## Current state (2026-09-22)
- **The DB no longer lives in the repo.** `src/db.py` resolves it from **`$PFF_DB`**
  (Windows: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\pff-data\pff.db`), falling back to `data/pff.db` when unset,
  so the Mac is unchanged until it sets the variable. Cause: `~/Desktop/DEV` is a two-way
  Google Drive mirror and Drive re-uploads and **locks** the 542 MB file on every write.
  `GoogleDriveFS.exe` held it open against a running pull. PR #1.
- **2026 pulled** (`run_pipeline.py --season 2026`): 1,614 games, 16,572 grades,
  1,252,863 stats, 39,960 premium; graded weeks 0-3. Baylor: 79 players over its 3
  played games, 17,215 snaps. Week 4 is 2026-09-26, so 3 games is complete, not a gap.
- **Machines now exchange Parquet, not databases** (PR #2). `scripts/export_snapshot.py`
  and `scripts/load_snapshot.py`, one file per table per season on Drive plus a
  manifest. The whole 612 MB DB is **40 MB** of Parquet; all of 2026 is 6 MB. A full
  snapshot of 2023-2026 is on Drive now, so the Mac can catch up without touching the API.
- **Mac loaded the snapshot 2026-09-22 18:15** and matches it (22 files, all counts equal;
  2026 checked row by row). Load bug found, data restored and the script fixed the same night (PR #4).

  `data/pff_before_video_plays_20260913_204343.db`.
- Full 2024 and 2025 seasons pulled (2026-09-13): 285,070 and 290,427 plays plus the
  games lists, `scripts/pull_season_video_plays.py`. Verified against the per-game pull
  (all 2,215 Baylor plays identical). Current equals legacy on 1.7% of plays, so the
  2024 model backfill happened. Consumed by PlayCalls_SuccessRate_EPA Phase 7.

  (all 2,215 Baylor plays identical). Current equals legacy on 1.7% of plays, so the
  2024 model backfill happened. Consumed by PlayCalls_SuccessRate_EPA Phase 7.
